question: Can the 2014 Apayao-Abulug River Basin master plan provide an authoritative freshwater spatial framework, and what access or source discrepancies must be resolved first?

masterPlanCatalog.title: Formulation of Integrated River Basin Management and Development Master Plan for Apayao-Abulug River Basin Volume 2 Main Report
masterPlanCatalog.pageAccess: The public catalog page exposes the title, publication year, file size and preview/download controls. The actual preview/download area displays Authentication Required, says login or registration is needed, and presents a required visitor survey before proceeding. No account was created, survey was not completed, and the PDF was not downloaded.
masterPlanCatalog.webToolAccess: Direct PDF retrieval returned a content-too-large error at 19,371,633 bytes. The catalog detail page was readable. This does not establish that a registered user may reuse the report or its maps.

searchIndexedReportExcerptReview.sourceLocation: Chapter 4, Table 4.1-1, titled Other important water bodies in the AARB; search-indexed PDF excerpt ends at Chapter 4-2
searchIndexedReportExcerptReview.reportedSystemContext: The excerpt describes the Apayao River as part of the Apayao-Abulug watershed and says the river is used for irrigation, power generation, communal fishing and transport. It also presents 18 other important water-body entries, each labelled Perennial Secondary in the excerpt.
limitations: This is text exposed in a public search-index excerpt, not an independently opened or reviewed copy of the complete report.
The listed functions are planning-document descriptions, not field-confirmed current habitat assessments or fish observations.
Headwater text is not a point coordinate, reach geometry, watershed boundary, or verified administrative crosswalk.
The excerpt does not identify fish taxa, sampling methods, dates, vouchers, abundances, or station-level occurrence records.
The 2014 report's map/data reuse terms remain unverified; login and a visitor survey are required by the catalog for preview/download.

officialSummaryComparison.pageType: FASPS E-Library catalog summary, not full report text
officialSummaryComparison.rankClaim: sixth-largest river system in the Philippines

officialSummaryComparison.pageType: Cordillera regional development council announcement endorsing the plan
officialSummaryComparison.rankClaim: ninth-largest river system in the Philippines
officialSummaryComparison.regionCoverageClaim: More than 90% of the described drainage area is in Apayao; the remainder, including the river mouth, is in Cagayan.

interpretation.areaAndRank: The two official public summaries conflict on drainage area (5,042 versus 3,372 square kilometres) and national rank (sixth versus ninth). The FASPS figures come from its catalog summary; only a search-indexed excerpt from Chapter 4 was reviewed, not the complete report or technical map. Do not select either as authoritative basin geometry until the report's technical map, hydrologic delineation, scale and datum are reviewed.
interpretation.crossRegionHandling: The basin is a shared L6 CAR/L7 Region II freshwater system. Apayao-only evidence must not be stretched to the Cagayan mouth or downstream reaches, and the basin must not be counted as completed for either region from this catalog listing.
interpretation.timeValidity: The plan publication year is 2014; the RDC page says the master plan horizon is 2014-2029. Treat historical development strategies and resource descriptions as time-bounded, not present-day status.

disposition.reason: The full volume is login/survey-gated in the public catalog, and accessible official summaries disagree on area and rank. A public search-index excerpt adds named river and stated fish-habitat planning leads, but no hydrologic map, complete report, or fish data was independently inspected.

nextAction: Request a public no-login copy or the authoritative basin boundary map and technical description, its CRS/datum and delineation method, sub-basin crosswalk, current revision, fish/aquatic survey appendices and data, and item-specific reuse terms. Validate each of the 18 names and its reported headwater/function against official hydrography and accessible field studies before further spatial or biological assertions. Keep CAR and Region II coverage linked but independently evidenced.
